title: Chapter 11 Mini-Capstone: Multi-Device Presence Priority & Routing Engine
solutionExplanation:
The presence router implements RFC 6121 priority routing:
1. upsert_session normalizes Bare and Resource components and replaces matching Full JIDs.
2. remove_session_by_pid implements an accumulator-based tail-recursive loop, cleanly pruning disconnected PIDs.
3. resolve_message_targets checks if TargetJid is a Full JID. If the exact resource is online, it delivers to that PID. Otherwise, it filters online sessions for the Bare JID where Priority >= 0, selects the highest priority (handling ties by returning all tied PIDs), or returns {store_offline, BareJid}.
4. broadcast_presence looks up subscribed contacts in RosterMap, adds the sender's other resources, dedupes PIDs using lists:usort/1, delivers the stanza via BEAM message passing, and returns the delivered count.

mentalModelCheck.question: When routing a message to a Bare JID (user@domain), how does RFC 6121 select the destination among multiple online client sessions?

options.label: It selects the session(s) with the highest non-negative priority (>= 0), or queues offline if all priorities are negative or no sessions exist.
options.explanation: RFC 6121 Section 8.5.2 specifies priority-based dispatch; negative priorities do not receive bare JID messages.

options.label: It broadcasts the message to every online session regardless of priority.
options.explanation: Messages are delivered to the highest priority session; ties result in multi-delivery.

options.label: It always stores the message offline first, then notifies clients via push.
options.explanation: Online sessions receive instantaneous BEAM message delivery.

options.label: It randomly picks an active socket PID.
options.explanation: Routing is deterministic based on integer priority rankings.
